In [[dynamical systems theory]], the '''Olech theorem''' establishes [[Necessity and sufficiency|sufficient]] conditions for global [[Lyapunov stability|asymptotic stability]] of a two-equation system of non-linear [[differential equation]]s. The result was established by [[Czesław Olech]] in 1963,<ref>{{cite journal |first=Czesław |last=Olech |title=On the Global Stability of an Autonomous System on the Plane |journal=Contributions to Differential Equations |volume=1 |issue=3 |pages=389–400 |year=1963 |issn=0589-5839 }}</ref> based on joint work with [[Philip Hartman]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=Philip |last=Hartman |first2=Czesław |last2=Olech |title=On Global Asymptotic Stability of Solutions of Differential Equations |journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=104 |issue=1 |year=1962 |pages=154–178 |jstor=1993939 }}</ref>

== Theorem ==
The differential equations <math>\mathbf{\dot{x}} = f ( \mathbf{x} )</math>, <math>\mathbf{x} = [ x_1 \, x_2]^{\mathsf{T}} \in \mathbb{R}^2</math>, where <math>f(\mathbf{x}) = \begin{bmatrix} f^1 (\mathbf{x}) & f^2 (\mathbf{x}) \end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf{T}}</math>, for which <math>\mathbf{x}^\ast = \mathbf{0}</math> is an [[equilibrium point]], is uniformly globally asymptotically stable if:
:(a) the [[Trace (linear algebra)|trace]] of the [[Jacobian matrix and determinant|Jacobian matrix]] is negative, <math>\operatorname{tr} \mathbf{J}_f (\mathbf{x}) < 0</math> for all <math>\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^2</math>,
:(b) the Jacobian determinant is positive, <math>\left| \mathbf{J}_{f} (\mathbf{x}) \right| > 0</math> for all <math>\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{2}</math>, and
:(c) the system is coupled everywhere with either

:: <math>\frac{\partial f^1}{\partial x_1} \frac{\partial f^2}{\partial x_2} \neq 0,
\text{ or } \frac{\partial f^1}{\partial x_2} \frac{\partial f^2}{\partial x_1} \neq 0 \text{ for all } \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^2.</math>
